strengths: Novel weighted Hilbert space L²(λ; R^d) framework providing elegant structural insight: row-stochastic matrices become self-adjoint while doubly stochastic ones accumulate κ²λ penalty terms, explaining convergence gaps beyond spectral gaps alone

Rigorous convergence analysis with tight, non-asymptotic bounds that clearly demonstrate superiority of Strategy II; closed-form spectral norm derivations (Prop. C.14) yield transparent constants; recovery of linear speedup validates framework

Actionable design principles translating spectral conditions to topology constraints via Rayleigh quotients; Corollary 7.3 provides simple degree-weight matching guideline (d_i ∝ λ_i) with constructive Algorithm 2

Comprehensive experimental validation across synthetic (least-squares) and real (CIFAR-10 ResNet-18) problems, multiple topologies, and network sizes (16-64 nodes); demonstrates Strategy II advantage even with smaller spectral gap
Clear, well-organized presentation with comprehensive appendix; intuitive explanations of technical concepts (e.g., consensus example in Section B.4); proper acknowledgment of scope limitations
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Algorithm 1 follows standard gradient tracking (Xu et al., 2017); modified Metropolis-Hastings matrix construction is well-known; main contribution is analysis rather than new algorithms

Restricted scope acknowledged but significant: undirected graphs only (directed graphs require beyond self-adjoint tools); single-loop GT framework (doesn't address acceleration); fixed heterogeneous weights (no time-varying analysis)

Tightness of main results unclear: condition in Theorem 7.1 with numerically-derived constant η ≈ 0.102 may be loose; step size constraints are conservative (e.g., α < 1/(λ_max β)√(1/(62B(ρ_J)))); necessity of conditions unknown

Theory-practice gap in experiments: step sizes chosen heuristically, not per theoretical bounds; CIFAR-10 reports loss/accuracy rather than convergence rates; topology design benefits (Algorithm 2) not quantified; no comparison with centralized/federated baselines

Practical applicability concerns: requires deliberate topology redesign to realize benefits; Algorithm 2 uses randomized trials with unspecified success probability; missing guidance on choosing ε (theory requires ≥1/2, experiments use 0.3)
